newsitem.title: UK: BAe shares up amid merger talk.
newsitem.headline: BAe shares up amid merger talk.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace advanced in early trade on Monday despite a report in the Financial Times newspaper that said merger talks with General Electric were close to collapse. The shares were up 16p at 12.76-1/2 by 0826 GMT while shares in GEC were 2p lower at 373p.
"The market is thinking that some sort of a deal is inevitable given the pressure from consolidation in the U.S." said Zafar Khan, industry analyst at SocGen.
The Sunday Times newspaper reported that the two UK companies were expected to enter talks about forming an alliance that could create a single defence equipment group valued at around 16 bln stg.
But the Financial Times said on Monday that merger talks had faltered on disagreements over asset values.
Shares in GEC were up 2p at 377p after initially opening lower on the day.
"Being the bigger party, GEC will have to make the offer and will end up paying the premium," Khan said. "Although it is difficult to see them paying a big premium for British Aerospace."
"The ideal situation would be to pool the defence assets of both companies into a new group but the problems will arise over valuations."

Elsewhere, British Aerospace is due to report annual results on Wednesday. Analysts expect the group to see pretax profits rising to around 417 million stg after exceptional items, compared with 234 million stg a year ago.
